newsitem.title: CUBA: Havana sending Cubans back to hometowns.
newsitem.headline: Havana sending Cubans back to hometowns.

text.p: Havana authorities have convinced more than 1,600 migrants from other regions of Cuba to return to their hometowns or farms as part of a campaign to curb uncontrolled migration to this capital of two million people.
Prensa Latina on Monday quoted Havana Mayor Conrado Martinez Corona as saying that persuasion was used "with the aim of of stopping disorderly migration" to the capital.
The article said that "more than 1,600 illegal (immigrants) left here without traumas ..."

Last week the Cuban government imposed restrictions on the migration of citizens from the interior of Cuba to Havana in a new law that also permitted returning many of those already in the capital to their home regions.

Authorisation to live in Havana must be given by the local governments of each of the city's municipalities. Violation of the law is punishable by heavy fines and deportation of the violators to the regions of origin.

The imposition of Cuba's first internal migration laws came after President Fidel Castro said that uncontrolled migration to Havana has resulted in unemployment, overcrowding, delinquency, shantytowns and insufficient resources to maintain the city's infrastructure.
Havana's mayor said it was difficult to calculate the number of persons living illegally in the city but Cuban sources estimated the total at several hundred thousand.
